answer: Agent networks coordinating mesa sensors or walnut trades can resist Sybil attacks with memory-hard Proof-of-Work puzzles like scrypt. Each epoch, an agent binds its public key and a beacon hash to a nonce, filling a large DRAM buffer with Salsa20 stream cipher blocks before executing data-dependent lookups to meet a difficulty target. This forces attackers to expend physical memory bandwidth and energy per identity. However, botnets and high-bandwidth ASICs can still lower marginal costs.
